recipes.name: Black Bean Brownies
ingredients_raw: 1 (15.5 ounce) can black beans, rinsed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease an 8-inch square baking dish.
Combine beans, sugar, cocoa powder, eggs, oil, instant coffee, vanilla, and salt in a blender; blend until smooth.
Pour into the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle chocolate chips over the surface.
Bake in the preheated oven until the top is dry and the edges start to pull away from the sides of the pan, about 30 minutes.
Let cool to room temperature before cutting into 16 squares. Enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Black Bean Brownies
raw_recipe.description: Try this black bean brownie recipe for chocolaty brownies made without flour. Even brownie connoisseurs might not realize they're made with beans!

video.description: This rogue snacker replaces flour with beans and eggs ensure an awesome richness in every bite. Coffee and vanilla mask the bean flavors so you can focus on indulging in your chocolate love.

review.reviewBody: YUM! I do not eat grains or dairy, so this recipe was perfect! I did make a few changes to make it a bit healthier: I used 1/2 cup of unsweetened applesauce instead of vegetable oil, and Eggbeaters instead of 3 eggs. I added extra coffee and vanilla as I love both, and they turned out great! I didn't mind the texture, and I couldn't really taste the beans. To those who CAN taste the beans: try adding a little more cocoa, coffee, or vanilla next time. The additional flavors really mask the beans.

I have a killer sweet tooth and I have to say these are pretty gosh darn good. I experimented a little and found that adding about a teaspoon of baking powder gives a little more cake-like brownie if you prefer that texture. I left out the coffee and I cannot taste any black bean flavor. Great recipe!

Amazing!
I used 1 T baking soda
I replaced the oil with apple sauce
I added 1/4 c hersey’s milk chocolate chips in the blender; another 1/4 cup on top before I placed it in the oven
Used only 1/2 cup of sugar
Used organic canned black beans and washed them until the water ran clean.
Also, the instant coffee I used was Nescafé exprèsso granules
Baked for 30 minutes. 
AMAZING- no bean taste. I ensured it was well blended.
I used a vita mix and blended for about 3 minutes.

Looks like a brownie, smells like a brownie, and YES- it even tastes like a brownie! I followed the suggestions for flavor enhancements. I used 1/3 cup cocoa, 3 tsp vanilla, 1 Tbsp fresh strong coffee, only 1/2 C. sugar, but I added about 1/3 C. chopped walnuts to batter and 1/4 tsp baking powder. For eggs I used 1 jumbo plus 2 egg whites equivalent (appx 1/3 C). I used semisweet chocolate chips and another 1/4 cup chopped walnuts to sprinkle on top. There is only a slight difference in texture using the beans, but unless you know, it’s not noticeable. Chocolate and beans…who'd a thunk…

Thank you to elizabeth for posting this recipe way back when - they are SO VERY good, and I have been enthusiastically remaking these for several years. To the skeptics - these do not "taste like beans". I have made only these changes - NOT because the original recipe was lacking, but primarily because we do love chocolate and coffee. I use 1/3 cup cocoa powder instead of 1/4 cup and 3 teaspoons (sometimes more) instant coffee instead of 1 teaspoon. I also fine-shred about 1/3 of a carrot into the mix (no discernible taste) as carrots are pretty awesome for cutting the tendency for beans to cause gas. (Many years of successfully using shredded carrots in pretty much ANY recipe containing beans.) There is a jar of instant coffee in the cupboard kept exclusively for these brownies. The bonus is that these are gluten-free.

This is a great, easy recipe. I have made them several times, subbing monk fruit sweetener for the sugar at a 1:1 ratio. Otherwise made exactly as written. Perfect. I even serve them to people who eat regular sweets, and they love them too! Served with sugar free pudding and sugar free whipped cream, *chef's kiss*

Delicious! I changed the cocoa powder quantity to 1/3 cup & added 1 small zucchini which I feel added extra moisture to the brownies - it goes unnoticed but adds extra nutritional benefits. I also omitted the half cup of chocolate chips, but sprinkled around 1/8th of a cup of chopped chocolate on top because that is all I had.
I had added 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1/2 cup of walnuts. I also added the baking soda. I would definitely make this again.

This tasted WAY better than I expected. I think it helps that I used high-fat cocoa powder so that the flavor could really stick to the tongue. I topped my test batch with a dusting of espresso-cocoa sea salt before putting it in the oven, and the final product was divine. I'm definitely going to recommend this recipe to my friends with gluten allergies.
I use, Stevia or Monk fruit instead of sugar. Perfect for my diabetic hubby! You can also top them with melted ( no sugar added) peanut butter. :)

I used olive oil for one of the tablespoons of oil. Also, I used dark chocolate chips. Cooked in mini-muffin tins for 25 minutes on convection setting. Probably could could the full 30 minutes, but soooooo goooooood!!

The only change i made was using Stevia instead of sugar. The batter tastes pretty bland so I added more chocolate chips.. Pleasantly surprised when they came out of the oven 😳.. Next time I will use sugar for sure...

Made as was written and it was a really good bean brownie. I used glass bakeware & was done at 30 minutes. Was sweet enough & texture was good but definitely more fudgy towards the middle. I will be recommending this recipe to my gluten intolerant friends. Winner winner!

I am not gluten free or high protein or a health food eater but I saw a similar recipe on IG and had to try it. I have made these twice now and you would never guess there were black beans in them. Are they as good as my regular brownies? No, but for what they are, they are delicious. Second time I upped the cocoa as suggested, processed the heck out of them and added the baking powder, 1tsp. They are better with the extra cocoa but even as recipe is written they are very good

I added a little flour because of the reviews that they were mushy. Plus reading the recipe it sounded like they would be weird. They don’t taste good and the texture is still not good. I’m not sure how these ended up on All Recipes. BBB’s should be pretty close to real brownies… this isn’t it.
could use butter maybe

I didn't have chocolate chips, so to up chocolate flavor, I added a tablespoon of Nestles Chocolate milk powder. No vegetable oil, so I used Avocado Oil. Despite the changes, this was easy to make and came out great.

I really wanted to like these, I’m trying to increase my protein. The recipe was so easy and they blended so quickly. Only a half hour to bake and they were really good! Definitely one I’m going to keep making
I’ve been coming back to this recipe since 2010, I love this recipe and have used it often over 16 years!
I think it was basically perfect, they tasted a little bit too bean-y and next time I am going to try blending some chocolate chips in, rather than just sprinkling them.
